notes.content:
[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28734688/2579a4c8a9f36a0f1bbf1075b714e15b19617e80.jpg[/img]

We thought you might like to know about our upcoming multi-tasking shooter for VR – [i]Shooty Fruity[/i]! The game challenges you to scan pack and serve whilst firing high octane weaponry at hordes of mutant fruit.  You can check out the latest trailer for the game [url=https://youtu.be/tuWkPIV7Hw8]here[/url].

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28734688/7853953f5d9e4406117d9d3394d69693d43e55a6.jpg[/img]

Coming to HTC Vive and Oculus Rift on December 19th, the game has been designed from the ground up for VR and motion controllers, and is jampacked with weapons, enemy fruit and power-ups across the numerous shifts in the game’s ‘career’ mode.  The game also features multiple tasks to do whilst shooting fruit, including checkout and the newly announce canteen.

[img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28734688/c39657d1ea822b1c84bd998db30d9da500ecc874.jpg[/img]

You can find out more information on the Shooty Fruity’s [url=http://store.steampowered.com/app/666100/Shooty_Fruity/]store page[/url], the [url=http://ndreams.com/titles/shootyfruity/]website[/url], or via [url=https://www.facebook.com/nDreamsVR/]Facebook[/url] or [url=https://twitter.com/nDreamsVR?ref_src=twsrc%5Egoogle%7Ctwcamp%5Eserp%7Ctwgr%5Eauthor]Twitter[/url]. notes.title: The Assembly Now Supports Oculus Touch Controllers
notes.content:
We announced a few weeks ago that we’ve been working on an update for The Assembly, which you may have seen already on Steam a few weeks ago [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/373650/announcements/detail/334785164998304623]here[/url]. The patch for Oculus Touch motion controller support is now live today!

Here’s a recap of what the patch does and doesn’t contain, as we want to be very transparent with the update’s content. The key element of the patch is how you’ll be able to use your Touch controllers as an input device for The Assembly, as well as enabling some key motion control mechanics.

[b]What you can do:[/b]
[olist]
[*]You’ll see the motion controls as your hands within the game. These can be used as an in-game controller, so you can select and interact with items and menu options. 
[*]You can reach out and interact with key objects in the environment, hold onto then, and inspect them closely.
[*]All the gamepad’s controls and buttons have been carried across, so you can now control your movement using motion controls. Just highlight where you’d like to move using the trigger, then you can blink to that location.
[*]We’ve improved The Assembly’s room scale by decoupling your look direction from your forward movement. [/olist]

[b]What you can’t do:[/b]
[olist]
[*]Because of the way the game’s underlying systems have been built, we were not able to add dynamic physics into the game. So, interactions are still digital. For example, you can’t fluidly open and close a drawer using your motion controls – you highlight the drawer, press the button, and it opens in front of you.
[*]You also can’t throw items around, or interact with every single object within the rooms and labs of The Assembly.
[*]The game was still originally designed as a seated experience and not a room scale one.  As such whilst it works great if you stick to the limitations of the in game environment, if you do want to try and break the game (e.g. walk through walls) it’s very much possible. [/olist]

If you’d like to see the Touch controllers in action, you can take a look at [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-qzkFJ6UUXk]this video[/url] with The Assembly’s Game Director.

You can find screenshots of the patch’s content on our [url=http://www.ndreams.com/blog/2016/the-assembly-now-supports-oculus-touch]blog.[/url]

We hope you enjoy the update, and please let us know what you think!

notes.title: The Assembly Now Supports Motion Controllers
notes.content:
We’re happy to announce that we’ve been working on an update for The Assembly to enable the game to support motion controllers. This also enhances your ability to play the game as a roomscale experience. It’s coming to HTC Vive tomorrow at 9am PT / 5pm GMT, plus Oculus and PSVR by the end of the year. Those later dates will be confirmed soon.

[b]Why Motion Controller Support?[/b]

As a VR developer, the community is very important to us. When we released the game a few months back we were delighted about many people’s enthusiasm for the game, however we received some criticisms from the Vive community for the lack of support for Vive controllers.
  
Until then we’d focused on making the game an accessible VR introduction across all the headsets and to us that meant gamepad as the primary input.  It was something we’d set out two years before the Vive was released (and before the Vive had even been announced), and while we delivered on this goal, the community’s passion for motion controllers had taken off during this time in a way we hadn’t anticipated.

Following the launch, we took this on board and looked at how we could best address the criticisms and this brought us to the motion control patch we’re announcing today.  We’d have announced it sooner, however we wanted to ensure the patch was final and submitted to Steam before we said anything, in case what we could do had changed and we under-delivered on our plans.

[b]The Patch[/b]

The patch allows you to use your motion controllers as an input device for the game, along with enabling some key motion control mechanics.  The functionality developed was chosen using the feedback from the community about what was most important, whilst focusing on what was possible without completely remaking the whole game.  We want to be very transparent as to what patch does and does not contain so have pulled together the below list.  You can also see this in action in [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-qzkFJ6UUXk&t=1s]this video[/url] we’ve made.

[b]What you can do:[/b]
[olist]
[*]You’ll see the motion controls as your hands within the game. These can be used as an in-game controller, so you can select and interact with items and menu options. 
[*]You can reach out and interact with key objects in the environment, hold onto then, and inspect them closely.
[*]All the gamepad’s controls and buttons have been carried across, so you can now control your movement using motion controls. Just highlight where you’d like to move using the trigger, then you can blink to that location.
[*]We’ve improved The Assembly’s room scale by decoupling your look direction from your forward movement.
[/olist]
[b]What you can’t do:[/b]
[olist]
[*]Because of the way the game’s underlying systems have been built, we were not able to add dynamic physics into the game. So, interactions are still digital. For example, you can’t fluidly open and close a drawer using your motion controls – you highlight the drawer, press the button, and it opens in front of you.
[*]You also can’t throw items around, or interact with every single object within the rooms and labs of The Assembly.
[*]The game was still originally designed as a seated experience and not a room scale one.  As such whilst it works great if you stick to the limitations of the in-game environment, if you do want to try and break the game (e.g. walk through walls) it’s very much possible. 
[/olist]

You can find screenshots of the patch’s content on our [url=http://www.ndreams.com/blog/2016/announcing-motion-control-support-for-the-assembly/]blog.[/url]

[b]Sale and Free Content[/b]

To celebrate the launch of the patch, The Assembly will be included in the Steam Thanksgiving Sale at 35% off. We’re also releasing some extra free content, which you can get if you’re a new or existing owner of The Assembly on Steam. This includes the official soundtrack, the script, desktop wallpapers, and a complete version of our behind-the-scenes video series. These can be downloaded for free on Steam tomorrow.

[b]Finally…[/b]

We’d like to say a big thank you to all of you who have supported the game so far and provided feedback on what we could do to improve the experience. We take feedback from the community seriously and hope that this goes some way to address the criticisms we’ve received around The Assembly.  The speed of innovation in VR is hugely exciting and is one of the reasons we love working in it so much.  However, it also means that, along with the rest of the industry, we won’t get everything right all the time over the next few years.  That’s why we value the VR community so much – listening to you is what makes us better VR developers.

notes.title: Patch 1.1.0 notes for The Assembly
notes.content:
Thank you all so much for your feedback on [i]The Assembly[/i]! We’ve just released our first patch which fixes a number of minor issues, and we’ve also updated our [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/373650/discussions/1/359543951705774275//]Known Issues[/url] to reflect this. 

As ever, if you experience any problems, please report them to support@ndreams.com or head over to our [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/373650/discussions/1/]Support Forum[/url].

We’re working hard to continue refining and improving [i]The Assembly[/i], so keep your feedback coming in. We look forward to sharing further updates with you soon!

[h1]Patch notes[/h1]

[b]HMD[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed an issue where camera re-centre option from oculus home menu does not work. 
[*]Fixed an issues where the application will crash if starting the game with SteamVR already working.
[*]Fixed an issue causing SteamVR to start when user starts the application in Non-VR mode. 
[*]Added Oculus runtime to the Steam version.
[/list]
[b]Global Audio + Subtitles[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed issues causing audio to fade when facing away from source. 
[*]Fixed issue causing dialogue to be attached to incorrect audio sources.
[*]Fixed global issue causing subtitles from secondary dialogue to be displayed over primary.
[/list]
[b]Global Lighting[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed general lighting issue that makes Dossiers appear unlit.
[*]Fixed general lighting issue that results in unlit desk draws.
[*]Fixed general lighting issue that makes Doors appear unlit until the player interacts with them. 
[*]Fixed issue with floating light in the waiting rooms in Chapters 5 & 7.
[*]Fixed issue where insides of drying ovens were unlit.
[/list]
[b]Global Graphical[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed streaming issue causing materials on Keypads to initially appear fuzzy.
[/list]
[b]Global UI[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed an issue where string references are being displayed when running on unsupported languages.
[*]Fixed issue where ‘Snap Turn’ control setting was incorrectly being displayed.
[*]Fixed issue that caused text to overrun its set boundary.
[*]Fixed issue causing unlocalised or string references are appearing instead of subtitles.
[/list]
[b]Chapter 1[/b]
[*]Fixed issue where tutorial prompt appears when player meets Chavez.
[/list]
[b]Chapter 2[/b]
[list]
[*]Adjusted the movement blink volumes within Chapter 2, so player doesn’t have to lean forward so much to interact with the Phone.
[*]Fixed Issue where wrong texture was applied to notepads.
[*]Fixed lighting issue where [spoiler]locker appeared black after picking up the keys[/spoiler].
[/list]
[b]Chapter 3[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed an issue that stopped progression on the maglev puzzle if player opens and closes the pause menu. 
[/list]
[b]Chapter 5[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed Corrupt texturing on scientist’s face.
[/list]
[b]Chapter 6[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed a UI issue where Nakamura’s nameplate appears on the screen after she has taken the elevator.
[/list]
[b]Chapter 10[/b]
[list]
[*]Added missing subtitles within the conversation with Adam.
[*]Fixed issue where McCoy’s dialogue is muted compared to Ming.
[*]Fixed audio processing on Cal’s audio so voice no longer has dramatic changes.
[*]Removed incorrect dialogue triggering when interacting with transport terminal.
[*]Fixed issue where picking up dictaphone in Chavez’s lab causes no-existent bird to start squawking.
[*]Fixed UI NPC name data for French and German languages – now displays the correct name.
[*]Fixed an audio issue where dialogue within the conversations with Adam overlay or are cut-off, in both French and German languages. 
[*]Fixed collision to kennel, so the dog food doesn’t fall through to cage below. 
[*]Fixed general UI issue that caused MEMO Unit to report player has entered into the wrong room.
[*]Fixed lighting issue where Director has strange lighting across his face.
[*]Fixed minor graphical and collision issues.
[/list]
[b]Chapter 11[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed graphical issue enabling player to see into the [spoiler]torture room[/spoiler].
[*]Fixed lighting issues on and around the MEMO box when player moves forwards/backwards.
[/list]
[b]Chapter 12[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed issue with Audio preference not being recognised in Chapter 12.
[/list]

notes.title: The Assembly is now LIVE!
notes.content:
We are excited to announce that The Assembly, our first major release for VR, has now launched and is available to purchase on Steam!
The Assembly is a first-person interactive story developed by nDreams for the HTC Vive and Oculus Rift, and is also available to play on flatscreen PC.
[url= https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=P_ywcq0-QxE]View the launch trailer here.[/url]]

[b]The perfect introduction to VR[/b]

The Assembly is a long-form, narrative-driven game designed from the ground up for your VR headset.  Freely explore intricate environments with accessible movement controls as virtual reality immerses you within the game’s world.

[b]What is The Assembly?[/b]

A mysterious organization known solely as the Assembly has been conducting secret experiments underground, their astonishing breakthroughs only made possible by operating outside government scrutiny and society’s morals. But what is the Assembly hiding?  

[b]Who are the main characters?[/b]

A chain of events threatens to expose this shadowy group.  You’ll play as two individuals – each with their own motivations – and discover the mysteries of the Assembly’s facility through contrasting perspectives. As newcomer Madeleine Stone, you’ll face a bizarre induction program that seeks to test your potential. And as veteran scientist Cal Pearson, you’ll make a series of shocking revelations that lead you to question the Assembly’s relentless pursuit of progress. Face thought-provoking dilemmas with uncertain outcomes that challenge your views of the Assembly and its members, and which come to a head in one of multiple thrilling conclusions.

[b]Got any questions?[/b]

Check the [url= http://steamcommunity.com/app/373650/discussions/0/358415738213606762/]FAQ[/url] first, then get in touch with us on the [url= http://steamcommunity.com/app/373650/discussions/]forum![/url]

[b]Need support?[/b]

Please contact support@ndreams.com if you’re having trouble. Replies will be in English, and live support will be available between 9AM and 10PM UK time on launch day.

notes.title: What to expect on The Assembly’s launch day
notes.content:
We’re only days away from [i]The Assembly[/i] launching on Tuesday 19th July [i](ooh, the excitement)[/i] so we want to get you mentally prepared for the mystery, exploration and moral dilemmas coming your way. Read on to find out what to expect, or [url=http://www.ndreams.com/blog/]head over to our blog[/url] to find out more about the game.

[h1]ADD THE ASSEMBLY TO YOUR WISHLIST[/h1]
Don’t miss out on the launch of the game, as well as any news, updates or community hot topics. Add [i]The Assembly[/i] to your wishlist to be notified when the game launches so you can crack out your headset and get started straight away.

[h1]LAUNCH TRAILER[/h1]
The launch trailer for [i]The Assembly[/i] is going live at 3PM UK time. The English version of the trailer will have Spanish, Italian and Russian subtitles, and French and German dubbed versions of the trailer will also launch at 3PM.

This post will be updated with links to the trailers when they go live on launch day.

[h1]LAUNCH TIMES[/h1]
The Assembly will begin to roll out across the world at 4pm UK time (GMT+1) on July 19th. Check the list below to see when [i]The Assembly[/i] launches where you are.

[b]UK + Western Europe:[/b]
HTC Vive, Oculus Rift and PC (all platforms): 16:00 

[b]Eastern Europe:[/b]
All platforms: 17:00

[b]USA:[/b]
New York, all platforms: 11:00
San Francisco, all platforms: 08:00

[b]Russia:[/b]
Moscow, all platforms: 17:00

[b]New Zealand:[/b]
Auckland, all platforms: 00:00 (July 20th)

[b]Australia:[/b]
Perth, all platforms: 20:00

Sydney, all platforms: 22:00

[b]Japan:[/b]
Tokyo, all platforms: 21:00

[h1]REVIEWS[/h1]
If you’ve not quite made up your mind yet, you can check out a summary of press previews on our [url=http://www.ndreams.com/blog/2016/the-assembly-press-previews-round-up-2016/]blog[/url].

You can also expect reviews to start going live from 4PM UK time on July 19th. These will pop up online in the hours and days after the game launches, so keep an eye out for those.

[h1]VR / NON-VR VERSIONS AVAILABLE[/h1]
[i]The Assembly[/i] has been built from the ground up for virtual reality, so players can experience the game in VR using an Oculus Rift or a HTC Vive. [i]The Assembly[/i] will be coming to PlayStation VR later this year.

However, to make the game accessible to all players, you can also play [i]The Assembly[/i] on a flat screen without using a VR headset.

So, there will be three purchase options on the Steam page:
[olist]
[*]The Assembly VR Bundle, featuring the VR and non-VR versions of the game. Upon launch, the player can select whether they want to play in VR or non-VR.
[*]The Assembly (non-VR PC version)
[*]The Assembly ‘VR Unlock’. This is the DLC component required to upgrade the non-VR version of the game to the VR version. Players must own the non-VR version of the game in order to purchase this. 
[/olist]

[h1]GOT A QUESTION?[/h1] 
Check the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/373650/discussions/0/358415738213606762/]FAQ[/url] first, then get in touch with us on the forum! 

[h1]NEED SUPPORT?[/h1] 
Please contact support@ndreams.com if you're having trouble. Replies will be in English, and live support will be available between 8AM and 10PM UK time on launch day.

notes.title: Behind-The-Scenes Developer Blogs
notes.content:
Hello! If you've been checking out [i]The Assembly[/i] and would like to dig deeper into its origins, we have a range of developer blogs which explore how the team crafted the game. Head over to our [url=http://www.ndreams.com/blog/][b]blog[/b][/url] for more, or click on the links below:
[list]
[*][url=http://www.ndreams.com/blog/2015/on-the-assembly-planning-for-the-unknown/][b]Producing [i]The Assembly[/i]: Planning For The Unknown[/b][/url] 
[i]The brave new world of VR game development has many tales of the unexpected.[/i]

[*][url=http://www.ndreams.com/blog/2016/designing-the-assembly-keeping-it-real/][b]Designing [i]The Assembly[/i]: Keeping It Real[/b][/url]
[i]How we threw away the Design rulebook and embraced real world principles for VR.[/i]

[*][url=http://www.ndreams.com/blog/2016/coding-the-assembly-lets-get-technical/][b]Coding [i]The Assembly[/i]: Let’s Get Technical[/b][/url]
[i]We share how we overcame obstacles related to reprojection to deliver a 3D UI in VR.[/i]

[*][url=http://www.ndreams.com/blog/2015/deconstructing-the-themes-that-built-the-assembly/][b]Building The Foundations Of [i]The Assembly[/i][/b][/url]
[i]We reveal the themes and inspiration behind our enigmatic VR adventure game.[/i]

[*][url=http://www.ndreams.com/blog/2016/the-assembly-creating-a-believable-world/][b][i]The Assembly[/i]: Creating A Believable World[/b][/url]
[i]When it comes to art, there are no shortcuts to building a life-like world in VR.[/i]

[*][url=http://www.ndreams.com/blog/2016/the-assembly-in-vr-hearing-is-believing/][b][i]The Assembly[/i]: In VR, Hearing Is Believing[/b][/url]
[i]We explain how audio, voice over and ambient music help bring the virtual world to life.[/i]

[*][url=http://www.ndreams.com/blog/2016/on-the-assembly-designing-for-virtual-reality/][b][i]The Assembly[/i]: Designing For Virtual Reality[/b][/url]
[i]We take you behind the scenes of the game’s development in our new video.[/i]

[*][url=http://www.ndreams.com/blog/2016/the-assembly-art-and-sound-in-virtual-reality/][b][i]The Assembly[/i]: Art & Sound In Virtual Reality[/b][/url]
[i]Take a further look behind the scenes of our upcoming game in our latest video.[/i]

[*][url=http://www.ndreams.com/blog/2016/the-assembly-telling-stories-in-vr/][b][i]The Assembly[/i]: Telling Stories In Virtual Reality[/b][/url]
[i]We unveil the voice cast and reveal story details for our upcoming VR game.[/i]

[/list]
We're releasing more behind-the-scenes blog posts for [i]The Assembly[/i] next week which we'll update here.

[b]UPDATE:[/b]

Check out our latest with [i]The Assembly[/i]'s Game Director Jamie Whitworth, who will take you through how we've improved [i]The Assembly[/i] since its initial demo in 2015. Read: [url=http://www.ndreams.com/blog/2016/improving-the-assembly/][i][b]Improving The Assembly's Virtual Reality[/b][/i][/url]
